course_name_en: Atatürk's Principles and History of Revolutions

learning_outcomes.text: To be familiar with the sources related to Atatürk's principles.
To have grasped the reform movements carried out in the Ottoman Empire.
To have grasped the historical foundations of Atatürk's principles.
To have a good grasp of the state structure of the Republic of Turkey.
To have grasped the situation of Turks in the 21st century.
To have grasped Atatürk's understanding of Republic and peace.
Understands the value of the Republic.
By delving into the historical roots of the Turkish revolution, consciously embraces Atatürk's revolutions.
Takes ownership of his state and nation, drawing strength from Turkish history and the Turkish national struggle.
Recognizes correctly internal and external threats to the Republic, secularism, and the Turkish nation, and remains vigilant against these threats.
Possesses a consciousness that understands his country, homeland, and nation, and produces appropriate policies for them.
Knows the difficulties experienced in the establishment of the Turkish Grand National Assembly.
Understands the difficulties of the National Struggle.
Analyzes what the Treaty of Sèvres brought.
Evaluates the gains obtained with Lausanne.

syllabus_topics: Atatürk's Principles and History of Revolution: content and purpose
Concepts of innovation and similar terms
Structure of the Ottoman State and causes of its dissolution
Efforts to save the state and reforms
Constitutional developments and intellectual movements in the Ottoman State
Geopolitics of the Ottoman State and its foreign policy against it
Administration of the Committee of Union and Progress and the final stage of the state
World War I and the Ottoman State
Armistice of Mudros and associated occupations, territorial demands from the Ottoman Empire and the Paris Peace Conference
Turkish nation's determination for independence and Mustafa Kemal Pasha
Mustafa Kemal Pasha's ideas and his transition to Anatolia
Congress Period (Amasya Meeting, Erzurum and Sivas Congresses)
Occupation of Istanbul, reaction of the Turkish people and other important developments
Opening and characteristics of the Grand National Assembly of Turkey
First activities and first laws of the Assembly
Reactions to the Assembly, internal rebellions, opposing communities, the press in the National Struggle
Fronts in the National Struggle: southern and southeastern fronts
Fronts in the National Struggle: eastern front and the Armenian question
Fronts in the National Struggle: western front, first occupations and national armies
Establishment of the regular army and financial resources of the national struggle
Treaty of Sèvres and its impact on the Turkish nation
Fronts in the National Struggle: First İnönü, Second İnönü, Sakarya Battles and the Great Offensive
Political side of the National Struggle: Armistice of Mudanya and Treaty of Lausanne, Turkish foreign policy during the Atatürk period
Revolutions in political, educational, cultural, legal and social fields
Atatürk's Principles (Republicanism, Nationalism, Populism)
Atatürk's Principles (Secularism, Statism, Revolutionism)

6. Atatürkçülük, I, II, III, Genelkurmay Başkanlığı, Ankara, 1983.
